newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: EU refinery output rises sharply in April.
newsitem.headline: EU refinery output rises sharply in April.

text.p: Refinery output in the 15 countries of the European Union plus Norway rose by 733,000 barrels per day (bpd), or 6.3 percent, to 12.369 million bpd in April, Stichting Euroilstock said in its latest monthly report.
Year-on-year, total output was up 284,000 bpd (2.4 percent).
Refinery crude intake in April was up 663,000 bpd (5.9 percent) to 11.897 million bpd.
This represented a utilisation rate of 90.13 percent, against 85.11 percent in March.
Gasoline production rose by 89,000 bpd (2.8 percent) in April to 3.318 million bpd, 60,000 bpd (1.8 percent) more than a year ago.
Middle distillate output was up 355,000 bpd (6.7 percent) in April to 5.645 million bpd.
Year-on-year, output rose by 258,000 bpd (4.8 percent).
Fuel oil output rose 135,000 bpd (7.8 percent) in April to 1.855 million bpd, which was 86,000 bpd (4.9 percent) more than a year ago.
Naphtha output, however, was down 11,000 bpd (1.1 percent) to 968,000 bpd, but was still 52,000 bpd (5.7 percent) higher than in April 1996.
They are based on a nameplate capacity of 13.2 million bpd for the European Union plus Norway. Refinery intake represents crude only and excludes natural gas liquids, feedstocks and other inputs.
